paper_metadata.title: Quantum Option Proﬁt and Loss Encoding for Risk Assessment

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum option risk assessment pipeline for European call options using QOPLE plus MLE-based amplitude estimation, evaluated in Qiskit on small instances with n = 3, 4, and 7 sampling qubits. It reports up to 99% accuracy, about 1% relative error at n = 7, and a theoretical O(1/ε) versus O(1/ε^2) scaling claim, along with at least 15% fewer ancillary qubits and 3x fewer controlled amplification operations than traditional QAE.

experiments.description: Quantum option risk assessment for European call options using QOPLE (option price loading, payoff encoding, cumulative PnL encoding) combined with maximum-likelihood-estimation-based amplitude estimation and binary search for VaR; evaluated on two European call option instances with varying sampling qubits.

algorithm.variant: maximum-likelihood-estimation-based amplitude estimation (MLE-QAE) for VaR estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: binary search until lmin >= lmax; MLE over amplitude-amplification samples
algorithm.parameter_initialization: not specified; amplitude-amplification sequence fixed exponentially and binary search initialized with lmin/lmax

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option expiration price distribution is discretized into 2^n samples and loaded into n qubits; strike price K encoded in a k-qubit register; payoff PnL encoded via comparator and auxiliary qubit; threshold l encoded in an S register for cumulative PnL comparison
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR such that P[PT <= l] >= alpha, where PT = max(ST-K,0) for call options
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary search over l; controlled comparison circuits; auxiliary qubit marks payoff region; no penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: European call option risk assessment under Black-Scholes-Merton lognormal price distribution

dataset_specification.description: S0=2.0, sigma=0.4, T=40/365, r=0.05; strike prices K=1.896 and K=1.5; price distribution truncated to ±3 standard deviations and uniformly sampled

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate ST to three standard deviations around the mean; equidistant sampling into 2^n points; fit linear mapping ST = 0.229*i + 1.209 for n=3 example; payoff mapping PT = 0.229*i - 0.687 for i > iK, else 0
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation in Qiskit; compare VaR against classical Monte Carlo with 10,000 samples; measure each l value three times and average; evaluate multiple n values and two option instances

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Truncate and discretize lognormal option price distribution; encode strike and threshold values into binary registers
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Binary search on l using estimated cumulative probability; compare quantum VaR to classical Monte Carlo VaR

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation for VaR estimation; same precision target
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed complexity is O(1/epsilon) versus O(1/epsilon^2); MLE is used to reduce circuit depth and auxiliary qubits while preserving quadratic scaling.
Paper states this as a resource reduction, not a runtime speedup; exact baseline circuit width is not numerically specified.

speedup_claims.conditions: MLE-based amplitude estimation with exponential amplification sequence
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-comparison claim from Table II; no wall-clock timing is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/ϵ) for amplitude estimation; binary search adds O(log2((lmax-lmin)/ϵ)) iterations; L loading described as O(2^n) in circuit complexity

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper reports only small simulated instances with n = 3, 4, and 7 sampling qubits
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper claims O(1/ε) amplitude-estimation scaling versus O(1/ε^2) classical Monte Carlo, plus at least 15% fewer ancillary qubits and 3x fewer controlled amplification operations than traditional QAE
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup is unlikely to survive fault-tolerance overhead under Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis
Circuit loading of the option distribution is nontrivial and likely dominates practical runtime
No end-to-end wall-clock advantage over classical Monte Carlo is shown

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports IBM Qiskit simulation and no real QPU/device name

num_qubits not explicitly given as a single total for the full QORA circuit; paper reports component register sizes (e.g., n=3 or 4 or 7 sampling qubits, P up to 2n+1 qubits, V up to 3n+2 qubits) rather than one fixed total circuit width
circuit depth not explicitly reported as a numeric value; only qualitative resource comparisons and query counts are given
The paper reports simulation results in Qiskit and compares against classical Monte Carlo, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage on hardware.
The claimed improvements are theoretical quadratic scaling and resource reductions, not a measured runtime win.
